heading: Indexed universal life in plain English (74 seconds)
name: What is indexed universal life? The plain-English version
description: Indexed universal life (IUL) is permanent life insurance with a cash value. Interest credits are linked to an index, but the money is not invested in the market. This short video covers caps, participation rates, the floor, policy charges and lapse risk. General education, not tax advice.
transcript: What is indexed universal life? Here is the plain-English version. Indexed universal life, or IUL, is permanent life insurance. It has a death benefit and a cash value account. The cash value earns interest credits linked to an index. But your money is not invested in the market. A cap is the maximum credit in a period. A participation rate is your share of the index gain. A floor is the minimum credit, often 0 percent. Caps and participation rates can change, within policy limits. Policy charges reduce the cash value. The floor does not stop those charges. Surrender charges may apply. An IUL can lapse if it is underfunded. Loans and withdrawals reduce the death benefit, and they can cause a lapse. Guarantees depend on the insurer's claims-paying ability. Illustrations are projections, not promises. An IUL is not a substitute for a retirement plan. This is general education, not tax advice.
